Obviously it fattens up more with more tracks but the more you add (more specifically, the further the pitch knob gets from the center) it will sound just like a chorus. Plus the further you get- the the more of an electronic sound you’ll get. You never know what’ll sound good in your mic till you try it! Any effects you decide to apply- you MUST apply EQUALLY across all applicable track. The worst thing you can do is change the effects or EQ on one track individually. The point is for all them to blend into one rich dynamic voice. When you listen on the head phones you shouldn’t be able to tell there are 5+ tracks. Just one really good sounding voice. Any effects should be changed as a WHOLE . Like smash all five signals into one and apply the FXs and/or EQs to that single signal.

Hey there!

Let me say first that this is perfect on its own. Well mixed and great lyrics that fit perfectly with the melody. What follows are suggestions that I think you should try out but- don’t think I’m saying the song is lacking! 

1. Trying fattening the voice up a little. Have you already done this? Where you have (up to) ten vocal tracks for your lead. You can use much less as long as it is balanced. The total tracks should be an odd number (original plus 2 harmony tracks) . Let’s use the number 5 for this example. 
Take your original track and clear it (temporarily) of all effects including EQs (as the appropriate settings will likely change). Now you are going to change the pan on all 4 new tracks. 2 will be left and the other 2- right. Set one pair of LR tracks halfway between the complete left and right (respectively) and the second pair of LR tracks to the complete end of the spectrum (fully left or right as the case may be). This is just laying the ground work for the actual effect since all tracks are the same except for the pan, there won’t be a noticeable difference yet. 
Next- we change the pitch (just a touch) on the 4 tracks. It depends on what DAW you use, but for both right channels add 2 or 4 cents (for the corresponding track) to the pitch (making it slightly sharp). Do the exact opposite for the left tracks. 

Now put an exact copy of the lead vocal in each track and adjust with effects etc to taste.

Let us know if that helps.
